Needs reviewPublishing outage root cause: live collection raised NameError on every run because scripts/originate.py used egw_live without importing itFour consecutive scheduled publish runs failed at "Regression tests" (40028653350, 40037957529, 40048429858, 40063011446) and the run for the merge of the time-bomb fix (40069088115) failed at the same step after 20 minutes. The GitHub annotation on that run names four tests, all reaching scripts/originate.py::live_collect, which referenced egw_live.EVIDENCE_NAME without the module ever being imported: every live collection raised NameError before touching any source, so no fresh snapshot could be published and the site served a snapshot older than its own eight-hour bound. Fixed in scripts/originate.py by importing scripts.egw_live and by moving the evidence-file unlink inside the guard so housekeeping can never abort a collection again; the four failing suites (tests/test_origination_upgrade.py, tests/test_f9d0a5a2.py) now run 39 tests OK. Second, independent cause of staleness: every merge to main starts a publish run, and GitHub cancels a PENDING run in the same concurrency group when a newer one arrives, so runs 40070626757, 40071009969, 40071100402 and 40071346040 were each cancelled while pending by the next merge. That is why a push-triggered publish rarely survives a busy merge window; the scheduled refresh uses a separate group and is the reliable path once this defect is fixed.

Needs review1 affected source recordsOwn network model: an explicitly uncalibrated last-resort line, priced only when the results graph clears every gateTo price fixtures where both sides lack an official rating and no book publishes a price, this session added a Bradley–Terry fit over bo3.gg finished series, expressed on Valve's 400-point logistic scale through teams that do hold official points. It is a research model, never odds. It fails closed on: fewer than 300 finished series in the graph, fewer than 10 anchored teams, fewer than 6 finished series for either side in the 120-day window, or a rating-difference one-sigma interval wider than 300 points. In the 2026-10-21T13:32Z run the graph held 4,605 usable series and 269 anchored teams. Zetta vs LOS NINOS still publishes nothing, and the diagnostic recorded why: Zetta (bo3.gg id 23468) is anchored on a Valve row and has 5 finished series in the window (needs 6), while LOS NINOS (id 25500) has no finished series in the window at all, so the fit holds no rating for it. Lowering the six-series threshold would therefore not price this fixture, so the threshold was left unchanged; the missing side, not the gate, is the blocker. The model publishes its ratings, sample sizes, standard error, interval and evidence hash on every row it does price, and the publisher replays the arithmetic before deploying.

Frozen-clock replay of the full suite at 04:50:59Z reproduced exactly one failure: tests.test_build.GlanceIndexTests.test_unresolved_fixtures_are_never_dropped_and_never_given_a_50_50 assumed glance() would always cap its synthetic rows, but the freshness-determinism guard's absolute pin 2026-10-20T12:00Z made the cap depend on the real time of day, so every run started on 2026-10-20 between about 04:01Z and 09:01Z failed. The test now uses an explicit synthetic time base (the repository's injected-time contract); frozen-clock replays at both failure instants pass 740/740, the failing module and the guard are green, and the production runtime (which never drops unresolved rows) was not changed. Full evidence chain: data/research/905fa4cf/production-gap-20261020.json.

It did not: egw_live.load_live had no caller. live_collect wrote data/origination/evidence/live-egw-reference.json on every refresh, while scripts/originate.py built the reference rung from reference_odds.load(), whose CAPTURE_PATHS was a fixed three-item allowlist of hand-reviewed captures. This session keeps no competing implementation; what it adds is integration cover - the rung is reached under the real collector, the whole chain replays to the same published number, a reviewed capture still wins, and a tampered or unwitnessed chain prices nothing (tests/test_a5b59ee6_publisher_wiring.py). NoticeReference replay used to select a capture by fixture id alone, which cannot tell a stale hand review from a fresh automated onebuild_origination.validate_origination replayed every published reference row against the first pooled entry carrying the same Hotspawn fixture id. Once the automated capture is in the pool, two captures can cover one fixture - and they can disagree, because a reviewed capture that has gone stale is skipped by the quote gate in favour of a fresh automated one. The audit would then replay the wrong entry and either fail the build or compare a quote to itself. Reproduced here and fixed on main by PR #270, which selects the entry by the provenance the published quote records (source_url, observed_at, excerpt_sha256) and asserts on it. This row is retained because the reproduction is independent evidence, not because anything is still outstanding.

Each row carries its own lock time and the summary marks locked rows; the register lists fixtures whose market never opened. Mitigation available but not applied here: a shorter refresh interval, at the cost of more queued runner jobs across parallel sessions.

Needs reviewThe downloadable snapshot served 2026-10-15 under a 2026-10-23 page (192.8 h apart) — fixed by publishing snapshot.jsonRunner read at 2026-10-23T09:58:24Z (run 39935447513, data/research/ca7e10e5/published-and-coverage.md): the public index.html carried data-snapshot-generated 2026-10-23T09:23:57Z, while the public /data/latest.json carried generated_at 2026-10-15T08:36:13Z. Every 'Open data ↓' and 'Full snapshot JSON ↓' link on the site pointed at that file, so a reader who downloaded it received an eight-day-old observation that contradicted the page above it. The same read at 09:51:40Z showed a 0.0 h gap, which proves the cause is the publishing race rather than a stale build: GitHub Pages is in legacy mode, so a push to main makes the platform republish the checked-in branch root, whose data/latest.json is the CI replay fixture. scripts/root_publish.py never copies data/ because replay and the regression tests assert against that fixture, so the root could not carry the current JSON. Fix: scripts.build now writes a byte-identical top-level snapshot.json, every page links and fetches ./snapshot.json, scripts.root_publish publishes snapshot.json into the branch root (data/ is still never copied), and scripts.verify_live plus scripts.acceptance_audit read snapshot.json first with data/latest.json only as a fallback for older deployments. Reproduce with tests/test_ca7e10e5_snapshot.py.

Needs review1 affected source recordsA two-way bookmaker quote of 1.00 / 12.00 is published as FlyQuest 92.3%; a decimal price of exactly 1.00 is not tradeable and needs the same rejection rule as a 1.8/1.8 placeholderThe published build carries fixture 1082860 (FlyQuest vs Staqued, DFRAG Invitational 2026, 2026-10-27T03:00Z) as a 'No-vig bookmaker estimate' from Thunderpick, with the observed price rendered as 'line 1.00 / 12.00' on Picks at a glance and 'Money-backed line / No-vig bookmaker estimate / Thunderpick' on the full audited list. The arithmetic is internally correct - 1/1.00 = 1.0000 plus 1/12.00 = 0.0833 sums to 1.0833, giving FlyQuest 92.3% and fair decimal 1.083 - but the input is the problem: a decimal price of exactly 1.00 returns no profit to a backer, so no book offers it on a live two-way market. It behaves like the identical-pair placeholders the ladder already rejects, and here it is not rejected because the pair is not identical and the implied margin (8.3%) looks normal. The effect is to publish a certainty-flavoured 92.3% on a fixture where no reader can verify a 1.00 offer. I could not re-read the original value: https://thunderpick.io/api/matches answered {statusCode:200, ok:true, data:{matches:[]}} when checked, so the collector's stored 2026-10-23T20:09Z quote is the only record of it and this flag is raised as needs-review rather than as a confirmed provider error. The other two bookmaker rows in the same build carry ordinary two-way prices (Alka 1.22/3.80 LOS NINOS and NEXVOID 1.60/2.17 Alter Ego), so this is one row, not the whole rung. Requested owner: the Thunderpick/Bovada paired-price rung (scripts/reference_odds.py and its callers) should reject any leg at or below 1.01 before margin removal, and publish the rejection reason the way the identical-pair gate does.

Needs reviewBranch-root publisher had to be restricted to HTML/assets and paired with post-push artifact re-deployLive verification of https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/MaltaProj3/unresolved/ at 2026-10-22T08:55Z returned HTTP 404 while the root index served 08:22Z HTML, exposing two publication hazards in scripts/root_publish.py and .github/workflows/pages.yml: (1) copying site/data/latest.json and site/data/origination.json into the git-tracked branch root without committing ~22 MB of data/evidence/ attachments breaks scripts.validate.check_data, validate_origination, and tests/test_contrarian.py on subsequent CI runs; (2) pushing a '[skip ci]' root-sync commit at the end of pages.yml triggers GitHub's legacy pages-build-deployment without running actions/deploy-pages@v5 afterwards, overwriting the full 24 MB artifact with the partial branch root. Fixed in scripts/root_publish.py and .github/workflows/pages.yml: root_publish now syncs only rendered HTML views, assets/, and .nojekyll (enforcing monotonicity via data-snapshot-generated in index.html and never touching git-tracked data/), and whenever root_sync pushes a commit, pages.yml waits for its legacy Pages build (--wait-legacy-sha), re-deploys actions/deploy-pages@v5, and re-runs scripts.verify_live.

Nothing here is wrong with any individual finding; the defect is presentation and vocabulary drift across sessions, and it makes the register harder to triage on a phone. Suggested handling for the owner of scripts/build.py (session arena-be019782 while PR #237 is open; this session did not edit other sessions' research files): render the recorded severity verbatim next to the badge (for example 'Needs review · recorded as low'), and state the mapping in one sentence at the top of the register. Everything below is an earlier session’s dated record. It is kept unchanged for provenance; the findings at the top of this page are the current ones.

Day-one review: 9z vs Aurora

Primary organizer result: — unverified. Secondary-source corroboration: HLTV reports 9z beat Aurora 2–0 at Thunderpick World Championship 2026, also listed on its match page. This is not relabeled as primary organizer verification. A historical prematch price was not captured here, so upset magnitude, closing-line value and retrospective pick accuracy remain — unverified.

What the report supports: HLTV describes 9z taking control on Inferno and Aurora struggling on Nuke. It also reports that Aurora had beaten 9z at EPL 24. That supports treating match-specific conditions as important, not assuming a prior head-to-head winner must repeat. This single result does not calibrate our model or establish a profitable contrarian strategy.

Aurora roster check — official dated snapshots

Valve’s 6 July snapshot lists MAJ3R, soulfly, Wicadia, woxic and XANTARES; its 3 August, 7 September and 5 October snapshots instead list Jimpphat, kyxsan, Wicadia, woxic and XANTARES. This verifies a difference in published roster listings, not the precise transfer/announcement date. The last three snapshots list the same five names. They do not confirm the match-day lineup, a change after 5 October, player onboarding, or the absence of a later change. Recent change date/player, rest and travel advantage: — unverified. The independently checked HLTV rebuild report attributes the additions of Jimpphat, kyxsan and coach ash to Aurora announcements. That secondary report corroborates the summer rebuild, not a new October change or its causal effect on this loss; no numerical probability adjustment is applied.

Fixed534-01 · publisher / regression gateThe four-hour publisher was blocked and the public site was frozen. The scheduled runs 39038670350, 39045650525, 39054246287 and 39058407711 all failed at the step 'Regression tests (repository fixtures, before any cache restore)' while the last successful scheduled run, 39031549764, completed at about 12:20Z. The cause was a single wall-clock-dependent assertion: scripts/build.py::shell decided staleness with datetime.now(timezone.utc) against a fixture whose inventory_observed_at was hard-coded to 2026-10-17T04:27:55Z, so the eight-hour freshness window closed at 2026-10-17T12:27:55Z. Because the regression tests run before the cache restore and before collection, that one expired assertion stopped every refresh.shell, matches_table, glance, summary, picks, coverage, scripts.build_origination.pick_row and scripts.build.build now take an explicit reference time, and one build passes a single reference time to every page. The wall-clock-dependent assertion pins its own reference time instead. New tests/test_freshness_determinism.py checks the injectability contract and re-runs the repository's time-sensitive test modules with the production clock pinned to four absolute instants that bracket the fixture which broke the publisher, so the guard keeps working regardless of when it runs; it fails on the old wall-clock form at three of the four instants.

The retained original pages for both final-day series show no published participants yet, because each is decided by the 17 October semifinals.scripts/twc_research.py::derive_day5 finds the two final-day series from HLTV's own page titles and their published start times, and scripts/build_twc.py::render_day5 publishes them with the verified Days 1-4 ladder that guides them. Platform limitationVD-04 · publishing / freshnessThe public site keeps reverting to the checked-in 15 October snapshot, because Pages is configured build_type=legacy with source main:/ and every push to main republishes the repository root. The checked-in root carries data/latest.json generated_at 2026-10-15T08:36:13Z (80 records, 17 upcoming), so for the ten-plus minutes the production workflow needs to collect, replay and build, the public site shows six-day-old matches and none of today's picks — and every new merge restarts that window, so while several sessions are merging the stale copy is what a reader usually gets. Observed repeatedly on 2026-10-22: at 01:30:26Z (eleven minutes after PR #146 merged), again after PR #150, and again at 04:25Z after the runs for d55ed87 and cd9a595 had been queued for more than half an hour, even though the workflow itself had deployed successfully (run 39717765225, both jobs success, 03:36Z). Two deployments of the same commit do conflict — the fixes that resolved that are described under handling — but fixing the deployment no longer stops the legacy build from overwriting the result.Three separate things were established and are recorded here rather than smoothed over. (1) The fast-republish job added in PR #150 deployed the same previous artifact first and made the fresh deployment fail at 'Run actions/deploy-pages@v5' in runs 39710589149, 39713153422, 39714834456 and 39715837365; deleting the duplicate artifact (PR #157) was not enough, and giving the interim artifact its own name was the change that worked — run 39717765225 for ea1534f completed with both jobs successful. (2) That still does not keep the site current, because the legacy build overwrites the deployed artifact on every push; the workflow's post-deploy guard detects that and redeploys, but a burst of merges keeps winning the race. (3) The only durable fix is a repository setting: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions (build_type=workflow), which needs an owner with Pages admin — the workflow token receives HTTP 403 from the Pages configuration API. Until that is changed, a reader who sees old matches should reload after the run finishes; the footer timestamp says which snapshot is being served.
